I think a nicer of handling multiple optional parameters is to pass them in an options "bag". This both allows specifying any one of the optional values (instead of all the values up to the one desired), and provides some self-documentation in the call.

e.g.
```
help.wrap(fullTest, 23, { minWidthGuideline: 20 })
```

Yeah, all the indents simply listed one after the other can be quite confusing, so I agree with you, except maybe `preformatted` should be additionally available as a separate argument, just like `minWidthGuideline` is now. Both are special because they are in essence universal settings that are supposed to have the same value in each call in any reasonable application, so ideally, they should only be used directly when overwriting `wrap()` in a subclass. Because of that similarity and since `minWidthGuideline` is already available as a separate argument, I think `preformatted` should be, too. We could also make them both properties of the `Help` class instead, so that the values could be configured with `Command.configureHelp()`.

Anyway, I got stuck trying to write JSDocs for the overloads with an `options` parameter. Apparently, VS Code does not understand overloaded functions well, so it led me to create this issue: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/187663.

The TypeScript is deliberately describing the most common cases. This signature is when you don't supply a coercion function, so are much more likely to be specifying a boolean or a string. (You can actually pass anything which is useful in rare cases, but if we describe that in the signature then we get no type checking!)

See #1119 for a lot of discussion, which led to the current signature.

I suggest the signature you want to be use in the TypeScript tests is the one with a coercion function.

@shadowspawn I see what you mean regarding the RegExp coercion function, but is that really the case if you don't supply any coercion function.

The TypeScript compiler produces an error for me when providing an object instead of a string or boolean, there is just no runtime checking.
@shadowspawn looks like I was confused, I see your point here.

Does the last overload ever get considered? Won't any overload that could match
`option<T>(flags: string, description: string, fn: (value: string, previous: T) => void, defaultValue: T): Command;`

already be matched by:
`option<T>(flags: string, description: string, fn: (value: string, previous: T) => (T | void), defaultValue?: T): Command;`

If I keep the current way your collector working:
- If the collector function return void, the defaultValue MUST be provide to store parameters, because, if not this option is useless an will be keep as undefined/void all the time.
- if default value is provided, so no problem the default value can be use as a storage, and the collector function can return void.

A couple of thoughts:
1) The regular expression support is no longer documented in README and soft deprecated. 
2) I am not sure if void makes sense, after experimenting tonight.

Would just two overloads work for all expected cases? (NB: this suggestion is untested as yet.)

```
option<T>(flags: string, description: string, fn: (value: string, previous: T) => T, defaultValue?: T): Command;
option(flags: string, description?: string, defaultValue?: any): Command;
```

(I think legacy code using regular expression will not cause a TypeScript error since will match signature of second overload. Untested,)
